title: Provider terms of use verified before building on them
Project name and license decided
Link one or more subscriptions per provider as profiles, each using the provider's official CLI with its own isolated configuration directory, detecting login status without reading credentials
Create an employee with name, role, system prompt, profile, workspace folder and permissions
Per-employee chat with streaming, history and immediate cancellation
Sensitive actions ask for approval, with a remember option per employee
Persistent memory per employee in SQLite plus Markdown notes, searchable
Each employee runs as an independent supervised CLI process in the background; several run in parallel and keep running when the window is closed
Desktop app for Windows, macOS and Linux: employee list, chat, approvals, profiles and tray
Daemon lifecycle on a personal PC: single instance, started on demand or at login, discoverable by clients, graceful shutdown

Only official CLIs and APIs, launched unmodified; never read, copy or forward subscription credentials; never rotate or pool profiles automatically
Each employee works in its own workspace folder with a scrubbed environment and a supervised process tree
Daemon startup to ready in under 1 s
Daemon adds under 50 ms to a turn, subscription time excluded
Streamed output reaches the client within 100 ms of the CLI emitting it
Daemon idle memory under 100 MB
Daemon binary under 50 MB
Resuming a paused employee in under 1 s
Windows 10/11, macOS (Intel, Apple Silicon) and Linux built and tested in CI; the daemon also built for Linux ARM64
Run the daemon on a VPS and connect the desktop app to it over Tailscale
Remote access only through the tailnet with Tailscale identity and an allow-list of users
10 parallel employees on a 2 vCPU, 4 GB VPS without degrading the interface
Shared threads where an employee delegates work to another
Scheduled tasks and triggers (cron, file changes, webhooks)
Browser per employee with an isolated profile
Skills as Markdown files with declared permissions, signed and reviewable
Change an employee's profile or provider without losing its memory
OS-level sandbox per employee (containers where available)
Learn a workflow by recording browser actions and the DOM, and turn it into a skill
Cost and usage panel per employee against each subscription's limits
Notifications when an employee finishes or needs approval
Multi-user, roles and shared memory
The desktop app manages several connections (this computer and VPS daemons) and works the same against each
Remote callers are identified, audited, and never allowed to share one person's provider subscription without an explicit, stored acknowledgement
